note: Catalog of inference backend downloads for Meridian Phase 11. URLs use the GitHub /releases/latest/download/ redirect pattern, so they always resolve to the latest published release. To pin to a specific version, replace 'latest' with the tag (e.g. 'b9835', 'v1.116.1'). All asset names, sizes, and SHA-256 hashes were verified directly against the GitHub Releases API on 2026-06-28. The 'hardware' field uses the vocabulary returned by backend_manager::detect_local_gpu_vendor (cpu | nvidia | amd) so the catalog can match catalog entries to the detected local GPU without a mapping layer.

backends.name: llama.cpp
backends.description: Reference C++ inference server for LLaMA-architecture models. Maintained by ggml-org, supports a wide range of hardware backends (CUDA / ROCm / HIP / Vulkan / SYCL / OpenVINO).

variants.label: CPU
variants.notes: Plain CPU build; no GPU required. Smallest llama.cpp Windows download.

variants.label: CUDA (NVIDIA)
variants.notes: CUDA 12.4 build for NVIDIA GPUs. A CUDA 13.3 build is also published upstream; we ship the 12.4 build for broader NVIDIA driver compatibility.

variants.label: ROCm / HIP (AMD)
variants.notes: AMD HIP/Radeon build for Windows. llama.cpp does not publish a separate ROCm-for-Windows archive (Linux AMD is shipped as llama-b<ver>-bin-ubuntu-rocm-<ver>-x64.tar.gz).

backends.name: llamafile
backends.description: Single-file portable inference server from Mozilla AI. One binary ships the entire model + serving stack; runs on any OS including Windows. Falls back to CPU gracefully when GPU init fails.

variants.label: Universal
variants.notes: Portable universal binary. On Windows, named without .exe by upstream — Meridian renames to llamafile.exe on install. Detects GPU on compatible cards and uses it automatically.

backends.name: koboldcpp
backends.description: Single-file pyinstaller inference server with built-in GUI. Supports LLaMA-derived models, image generation, and TTS. CPU-friendly defaults; Windows AMD path goes through Vulkan on the nocuda build (per upstream README).

variants.label: CPU / Vulkan
variants.notes: No-CUDA build. Supports CPU inference and Vulkan — recommended for AMD GPUs on Windows per upstream.

variants.label: CUDA (NVIDIA)
variants.notes: CUDA-enabled build for NVIDIA GPUs (largest Windows asset in this catalog).

backends.name: TurboQuant
backends.description: Drop-in fork of llama.cpp maintained by AtomicBot-AI, bundling the TurboQuant quantization pass and TriAttention KV-cache pruning. Same CLI interface as llama.cpp plus --triattention-* flags. Windows tags ship as flat zips (no parent dir) so Meridian uses zip-flat extraction.

variants.label: CUDA 13.3 (NVIDIA)
variants.notes: Primary NVIDIA path. Requires CUDA 13.x runtime on the host. Pinned to tag d86eb0b (cannot use /releases/latest/ — AtomicBot-AI publishes a different tag per variant).

variants.label: CUDA 12.4 (NVIDIA legacy)
variants.notes: Older CUDA 12.4 build for hosts that have not yet upgraded to CUDA 13.x. Largest of the four variants (~682 MB).

variants.label: CPU
variants.notes: Plain CPU build — no GPU required. Smallest turboquant Windows download (~11 MB).

variants.label: Vulkan (AMD / fallback)
variants.notes: Vulkan build for AMD GPUs on Windows. Also used as a generic fallback when nvidia runtime missing.

backends.name: Lemonade
backends.description: Embeddable ONNX runtime from lemonade-sdk. Single binary auto-detects NVIDIA CUDA / AMD ROCm / Intel NPU / CPU at startup; exposes an OpenAI-compatible API at localhost:13305. Tier 2 — brings medium-sized GGUF + ONNX + FLM model support with AMD NPU acceleration. Apache-2.0 licensed so Meridian can bundle it freely.

variants.label: Embeddable (Windows x64)
variants.notes: v10.8.1 pinned. Single-binary embeddable runtime — the same binary auto-detects NVIDIA / AMD / Intel-NPU / CPU at startup, so one row covers every host. Hardware marker is 'cpu' so the auto-picker keeps this as fallback when no vendor-specific match exists. SHA-256 placeholder; replace after the bundle is verified.
